FearoftheUnknownStart.4.full: It is with great reticence that I relay a grievous event which occurred upon my arrival. It is my hope that in penning these thoughts my mind will find solace from the foul images that have so firmly embedded themselves.

FearoftheUnknownStart.5.full: I will spare you the details of the journey to that dismal village to settle my deceased father's affairs. But upon entering its unpaved limits, my spouse drew my attention to several men and women galloping towards the town center, where there was a loud commotion and gathering of individuals. Intrigued by the local pageantry, I resolved to indulge my curiosity. I rapped my knuckles against the roof of the carriage and asked for the driver to turn towards the festivities.

FearoftheUnknownStart.6.full: He did not respond to my insistence. Nor did he respond when I thrice repeated my command. Frustrated, I angled my head out of the carriage window in order to speak more firmly. That is when I spied the horrific source of his obstinate and wise decision. For the briefest of moments — though a moment long enough for it to be etched within my memory forever — I saw the source of the commotion: A crowd of people surrounded a tall wooden stage where, swinging slowly from a thick hemp noose, hung a youthful woman. Her lifeless eyes stared in my direction before her form was obscured by buildings.

FearoftheUnknownStart.7.full: An irrational fear has gripped the populace. I swear it. The region is rife with superstitious traditions; traditions that do not mix well with the Church's rigid moral compass. When an individual from this close-knit community emerges from shuttered windows, they eye me as one would a foreigner, with sideways glances that make each excursion there insufferable. Accusations of witchcraft and voodooism erupt with increasing fervor, and paranoia weaves its tendrils into their minds.

FearoftheUnknownStart.8.full: Maybe this forced solitude will prove beneficial to my wits, as even amidst this clamor I find myself unnaturally focused. I have recently discovered my father's leather-bound journal and, while somewhat trite, I feel it has sparked something within me; a direction for my future studies, perhaps. Maybe it will offer some amusement in these trying times.

S4Kill1.3.full: It is nearing midnight now, and I struggle to find my words. Is this remorse I feel, or elation? Even as I was swept into the midst of the frightened crowd, watching the flames swirl upwards, I was spellbound by their savagery. I could not imagine that this paranoia would be exercised so bluntly!

S4Kill1.4.full: It began over supper with my siblings: **The Blacksmith** - accused of practicing witchcraft - was carried past our brasserie to the steps of Town Hall. He wailed and protested his innocence, and when allowed use of his hands, he immediately accused Henriette, the town **Butcher**, of beguiling him. Within moments, he dramatically convulsed and acted as if under a trance when she decried his accusation.

S4Kill1.5.full: As we investigated the commotion that had interrupted our dessert course more closely, the **Blacksmith's** eyes blazed with fiery determination. He pled with us specifically. He would offer us his services, whatever we needed to spare his life.

S4Kill1.6.full: The **Butcher** was pressed to the steps of Town Hall. Silent, innocent as she approached, and forlorn. We knew that Henriette would offer the same deal.

S4Kill1.7.full: There was no way to slake the public's thirst for catharsis without bloodshed. Tonight, a witch was burned.

S4Blacksmith.3.full: Though a ghastly event, it was perhaps fortunate. As the blaze extinguished and the crowd dispersed, no eyes cast their suspicious gaze upon myself, nor my cousins.

S4Blacksmith.4.full: Henriette was exceedingly appreciative of our vote of confidence and offered us a discount on her services. No questions asked.

ForeignIntro.4.full: I hope you will forgive the direct manner in which this letter is received. Due to recent events, I no longer entrust my correspondence to postal carriers and prefer to hire discrete private couriers. This message is meant for your eyes only and I will not allow those who so blatantly scheme against me an opportunity to uncover my motives!

ForeignIntro.6.full: I have only just been situated these past few months with my spouse and close servants, and scarcely familiarized myself with the thatched-roofs and bucolic scenery, yet already I have seen the fires blaze at night, the screams of the damned, and the gibbet creaking under the weight of swinging bodies. The mob comes with torches in the evening and rips the accused from their residences. It appears that my parent's warnings proved true. The occult hysteria that they endured has returned in earnest! I fear that I may be next!

ForeignIntro.7.full: Even my own cousins have begun to eye me like mongrel dogs, yearning for scraps. In their jealous mania, they wish to uncover my secrets and claim them for their own. I can see how they desire to place the blame upon me; to distract me from completing my family's important scientific work! It would break my heart to see ill come to them, yet if they continue in their provocations, I will not hesitate to unleash the fires of hell upon them.

ForeignIntro.8.full: But I am secure in my ambitions. I have uncovered my true purpose. I will not succumb to fear. My secret work consumes my waking hours and I will stop at nothing to see it come to fruition!

CreatureIntro.4.full: As mariners are wont to say; there is always a lull before the storm. As I am wont to say; a lowering of barometric pressure generally occurs before the storm. And this idiom certainly applies to the horror of my current situation.

CreatureIntro.5.full: My family's manor is set on a small precipice, its imposing iron gate emerging from the forest like the mouth of an otherworldly beast. You have no doubt seen the daguerreotype, so I will not delve further into detail. I remembered the daunting architecture from my youth, and returning to claim my inheritance left me feeling trepidatious.

CreatureIntro.6.full: Whatever the cause, it appears the delirium of the past has ebbed and conversations about the darker history of the town are now relegated to whispers in private. The consensus is that justice has been served and modern living has prevailed over the old ways. In fact, there are many who deny that the events occurred at all.

CreatureIntro.7.full: The underlying symptoms of mass hysteria have channeled themselves into other menial and unproductive modes of thinking. I am of the opinion that they overcompensate for the shames of their past. While the ground has just been broken, the district has invested in the most modern alienist philosophies — absurd and untested as those theories are — and a new Asylum is being constructed to focus on the rehabilitation of the mind.

CreatureIntro.8.full: So, like a wolf licking its wounds, the town has returned to a relative peace. And for a moment, it seemed that the calm would provide a welcome atmosphere to return to my labors.

CreatureIntro.9.full: That is, until the Creature appeared in my window one night, it's bulky frame wet with rain.

S4Jail2.3.full: Is it true they have plans to convert the Asylum into a private penitentiary? If I were to venture a guess, I would assume **your investments** may have had a hand in it.

S4Jail2.4.full: Well, I say good riddance. The thought of spending precious resources to reform a mind already lost when they could be put to better use manually. It is like trying to unrotten a rotten fruit!

S4Jail2.5.full: Since your last letter, I have heard rumors that with **generous financial backing** from some anonymous donors, they are expanding the Asylum. Given your disposition, I would not be surprised to discover that you had a direct hand in it.

S4Jail2.6.full: I say it is a positive thing, this mental rehabilitation. I've always been intrigued by the potential of the human mind both to adapt and to be adapted upon. Though, I suggest you keep your distance. They may mistake your jocularity for insanity and admit you. Wouldn't that be something?

IsolationIntro.4.full: I tell you, these damn peasants actually built a wall around their own town. In the 1800's no less! These fools have traded paranoia for utter delusion!

IsolationIntro.5.full: Do they expect a foreign government to set up a military line and trebuchets to lay siege to this backwater stronghold? What on earth would it offer them? Trade has suffered. Prices have risen. And most importantly, with the caravans left to go elsewhere, I must find alternative ways to procure knowledge.

IsolationIntro.6.full: Why just this week, I was enraged by the audacity of the intrusion into my affairs! I, the rightful heir to a considerable estate, was forced to suffer the indignity of a physical inspection at what appeared to be a freshly fashioned gateway to the village where I was born. And then, to infer that I was bound by duty to prove my citizenship? My spouse was so manhandled that they were forced to spend the next week in their bedroom consumed by anxious thoughts.

IsolationIntro.7.full: Curse this infernal world filled with frustrations and complications at every turn! If only these regressive tendencies toward isolationism could have been resolved in another way! Surely, you can determine how dire the situation has become if it has rattled my notoriously pragmatic disposition. How can one change the world when it so decidedly wants to remain the same?

IsolationIntro.8.full: Mark my words, I would sooner watch these ramparts crumble than allow them to destroy my spirit. I will find a way to circumvent this oppressive state and preserve my legacy at all costs!

TensionIntro.4.full: Ah, what relief it is for one to not spend each waking moment fearing they will be burned at the stake! The oppressive hostilities of the Romanian countryside, of which I had become familiar during my youth, made the anxiety of my carriage-bound return to the old estate a dreadful prospect.

TensionIntro.5.full: Yet, even as the ink dried upon the executor's paperwork, my spouse and I quietly enjoyed our coffee against the bustle of a cobblestone street. The only eyes upon us were those clearly impressed by our bright, Parisian attire. Never once did an errant gaze suggest I would be shot with a revolver or murdered viciously by a stiletto. It was almost disappointing.

TensionIntro.6.full: With the town's decision to forgo construction of a barrier, the emergence of additional trade and the ceasing of xenophobic hostilities has allowed further interaction with other cultures. I find myself entertaining exotic guests that pique my darker interests. The occult and its superstitious effects on my family's past has become a peculiar fascination. Spiritualism being the fashion these days, you know.

TensionIntro.7.full: However, "old habits die hard" as the saying goes, and a delicious tension roils beneath the surface of the town. Acceptance (or apathy) may have calmed the tempest of hatred, but I realize that this deep psychological infection has yet to be fully reconciled. With each visit, I feel my actions push these factions closer until they will be forced to make a potentially devastating and amusing decision.

TensionIntro.8.full: It is an experiment in itself; a powder keg waiting to go off. And I am desperate to observe the results.

PrivatizedIntro.4.full: I will keep this letter brief — as brief as I can. You are aware that brevity is not my strongest suit. However, it is August, the ink struggles to dry in the humidity, and my mind is set on complicated things. Perhaps it would be more amiable to pen this missive in my own blood, cold as I am perceived to be by the inhabitants of this gray, lifeless city. It would certainly bring a little more color to it.

PrivatizedIntro.5.full: You are probably interested in matters of business, and it is going exceedingly well, or so I hear — I struggle to keep the figures in my head. I, and regrettably my good cousins, whom I love dearly, have invested directly in the town's well-being and now own a substantial portion of the commercial district. It appears that my parent's investments have paid off handsomely.

PrivatizedIntro.6.full: News of the day: The Asylum Project, which I believe was misguided from the beginning, has become a more intriguing source of labor. It's not that I believe that rehabilitation of the deviant mindset is impossible, it simply requires a more aggressive therapy than they were willing to indulge. With our unmediated assistance and the endorsement of the state, a prison is a more versatile testing ground.

PrivatizedIntro.7.full: And I — I am doing well. It disconcerts me. My studies continue with great passion that consumes me more than anything I have ever known. Even the dismal fog that looms across this bleak valley fills me with a solemn peace. Yet it is that same calm which causes my unease.

PrivatizedIntro.8.full: I must work quickly, as I feel something unseen watches, waiting to emerge from the shadows. I cannot have destiny torn from my grasp just when I reach the pinnacle!

LiberalIntro.4.full: I apologize for the tardiness of my reply, but settling the matters of my inheritance has uncovered distressing revelations that haunt my waking hours. It is terrible. And by terrible, I mean decent, cheerful, and painfully dull. People stroll around this inviting town, greet each other with smiles, and share baked goods. Baked goods! How are they so blind to the dark realities of the world? How did we arrive at such an excruciatingly positive conclusion?

LiberalIntro.5.full: While other institutions across Europe experienced the ravenous strain of overcrowding, our town’s well-funded lunatic asylum proved a luminous model of rehabilitation. Restraints were traded for personal care from the staff and a work release program was expanded for patients eager to assimilate themselves into society once again, with the skills to succeed.

LiberalIntro.6.full: It is an interesting concept in theory, but one which we know will only end in folly. When I made a brief visit to the Asylum Program (as they now so boldly call it), they even attempted to evaluate me as if I had been admitted. Apparently, the country has turned to more civilized ways to disenfranchise individuals that they fear — not to mention the additional taxes levied against legitimate entrepreneurs such as myself.

LiberalIntro.7.full: Like mighty Atlas, I will accept these heavy charges. While I disagree with their methodology, and the expenses of this progressive approach will certainly be a financial burden, access to skilled labor does appeal to me from an efficiency standpoint, if they have the stomach for it.

LiberalIntro.8.full: The days are certainly bright here in the valley, but in the end, this light will only make my family's work shine more brilliantly!

S4Jail1.3.full: Your previous letter appeared rushed and ended with incoherent scribblings. What is this creature business and why have you failed "in the eyes of god" by **aiding the poor thing**? Are you quite sure about your own mental state?

S4Jail1.4.full: I have heard a rumor that the **Asylum has expanded**. Perhaps your recent bout of good will spawned this charitable fortune. Whether it is so or not, my friend, I would refer you to it. Not necessarily by way of admitting yourself - unless you feel obliged - but perhaps they could recommend you a remedy to calm your thoughts. I suspect you may require more than a spot of tea and bed rest.

S4Jail1.5.full: What is this nonsense I hear about a hideous **creature left stalking about the countryside** in your region? I ask you only because your recent letters about experiments have been quite unforthcoming.

S4Jail1.6.full: I may disagree with your methods, but I have always attempted to stand by you as an academic. Allowing a monster to wander through the land unchecked, and by many accounts stealing and murdering along the way; why I believe this is sufficient grounds for which to end a friendship.

Witchwolfresolution.2.full: Word travels quickly in these parts. For as distant I am from the civilized world, I am equidistant from any meaningful activity to gossip about. While I'm sure you have heard of the recent family tragedy, I wanted you to read it from my own words.

Witchwolfresolution.3.full: As cousins, we frequently sup together when time and weather allows. But woefully, one occasion we chose a night where the wind howled remorselessly and set the locust trees to rapping against the estate windows. Upon this uneasy evening, we spied a great light beaming from the forest, and soon a throng of townspeople rallied around the exterior walls, waving torches and brandishing pitchforks.

Witchwolfresolution.4.full: The townspeople blamed us for bringing a blight of witchcraft upon their town. Tonight, they demanded a sacrifice and no amount of persuasion would slake their thirst for blood. As the hounds kept them at bay, we were forced to make a sanguine decision that would haunt us for the remainder of our days.

WallEvent.2.full: As expected - and as I've relayed to you so amusingly in the past - the town is not seeing adequate support for their memorial. This time, however, I was distinctly unamused to have my experimentations interrupted just as I had secured a moment's peace. Only yesterday, well-dressed representatives from the local government (mind you, as well-dressed as a fop with a decade's old sense of fashion can be) visited the estate in person to ask for my assistance.

WallEvent.3.full: When I pressed as to the actual purpose of our donations, they act as a parakeet with its cage door rattled; wildly gesticulating and talking vaguely about eliminating all possible superstition and influence from the town to make it prosperous again. Quite unlikely, I would say.

WallEvent.4.full: My dealings with the local Romani merchants have made it clear that whatever the town's petty inclinations, the memorial will have a deep affect on their trade. The Romani do not wish to leave the region, but will do so if pressed.

After the untimely death of several of my cousins' mutual business partners, and the appearance of blood pentagrams at various locations within town, even I began to find it suspicious. Was it a supernatural manifestation – a dark power willed to one of us – or mere happenstance?

WitchIntro.4.full: We also could not overlook the possibility of the {0} perhaps enacting a misguided sort of vengeance with the entire affair. I had noticed them skulking about during my early visits to town and the events of decades past clearly weighed heavily upon them.

WitchIntro.5.full: While the townspeople squabbled over superstition, we, intellectuals, decided to put the scientific method to good use in order to determine which of us had become cursed.

Instead, I waited upon my veranda, watching the city seethe in the valley below until my tea grew cold.

But, moments later, I saw the beating of the animal's once-dead heart as it began to struggle against its bindings! Life from death!

EssentialCons.3.full: Whether for love or purpose - I know not which drove my decision - I broke into the mausoleum housing my spouse and applied the solution to their skeletal features. *Following the exact recipe for the formulae proved difficult, but I was able to make due with local alternatives.*

I believe - as an anonymous and unbiased person without any scientific background - it is of utmost importance for us to push past these ridiculous preconceptions and expand our acceptance of new ideas.

JailEvent1.4.full: A man stepped forward to the cheers of a throng of miscreants. The man was strong and rough with a ruddy complexion, a broad, square jaw, and a beard separated by deep scars along his cheeks. He wore a thick apron with one shoulder strap ripped at the seams. The front was covered in dark stains, and by his confident stride, he seemed to revel in its uncleanliness. In his gloved hand, he held a hammer which dripped with a red substance that also stained his fingers.

JailEvent1.5.full: A woman stepped forward to the cheers of a throng of miscreants. Her hair was cropped shorter than a bob, dark and wild with a sheen of oil. It framed her angular face and draped over a black eye-patch that covered her left eye. She wore a thick apron that was once white, but now stained a dark crimson with fresh droplets of red bespattered across the chest. In her gloved hand, she held a metal cleaver, rusted near the handle, with thick divots in the blade from years of use.

JailEvent1.6.full: "They call me {0}. Perhaps you remember my family, and how they were ruined by the accusations of hysterical peons so many generations ago. Well now, us unfortunate wretches have taken back what is rightfully ours. {1} runs this town."

JailEvent1.7.full: The aberrant horde roared their approval. The malcontented rabble beat their chests and clattered metal upon metal.

JailEvent1.8.full: I spied a shadowy figure within the Junk Palace, its distorted silhouette framed against the entryway for a moment before disappearing once again. Was this the same creature I had hunted for?

JailEvent1.9.full: "I have brought you here because you are useful. But mark my words, {0} expects loyalty."

JailEvent1A.3.full: While I despised this cretin for their signature treatment of me, I also felt a strange sense of pride that my experiments had been appreciated, even by one so base. {0} commanded an authority that I could not help but admire when the fear of immediate death had left me.

Prologue-FOTU.3.full: I have made much progress in my research over these last months. My host has furnished me with appropriate accommodations and the food is hearty with a warmth that lifts the spirits. While I am gracious for their hospitality, I have yet to give my appreciation in person. The caretaker assures me that they are on extended holiday, but their absence is peculiar. Something about this arrangement unnerves me, though I cannot for the life of me determine its source.

Prologue-FOTU.4.full: It is but a minor xenophobia, a fear of the unknown that sets my eyes to dwelling on the dark corners of this unfamiliar, decaying, but immaculate estate. At night, I perceive to hear the echoes of a distant hammering, the scraping of metal on metal, the rumble of thunder. Yet when I sash my nightgown tight and emerge upon the veranda, the misty countryside is spread wide under the moon and I am greeted with nothing but the echo of cicadas and the smell of tulips in the night air.

Their contents are fascinating and I have arranged them in a semblance of order which tells a vivid, extraordinary tale.

Prologue-FOTU.6.full: I expect to return to London shortly, but I have posted this ahead of my arrival so as to make the burden lighter for me. I fear I don't have the same fortitude that I once did. If perchance something were to happen to me, I trust you will ensure its publication in whatever form you see fit.

Prologue-FOTU.7.full: As always, I think of you fondly. Give mother my warmest regards.

Yet, here I write to you in haste with a fire to my diction. These cretins would penalize us for our very existence! They eye us with such apprehension that it preys upon my anxieties at every stretch.

Creepy1stPlayer.5.full: A pox on their wild superstitions! Oh, how I wish I were back in university!

Creepy1stPlayerB.3.full: The burden of fame has finally pressed its weight upon me. It is obvious from the awestruck silence upon my visits, that my cousins view me as an unrivaled inspiration and this sentiment has seeped into the mindset of the burghers as well.

Creepy1stPlayerB.4.full: While it vexes me to lose time to matters of local import, I cannot fault them for their inquiries. With the paranoiae of the past fading and my exemplary leadership on display, it is only natural. My affluence is my curse.

Creepy1stPlayerB.5.full: What a bother it is to be so popular.

I noted how strange it was that my brief recollections of him as a child proved to be spot on. While my parents had passed, the Count seemed to have never aged a single day. The benefits of a healthy disposition and good living, I suppose.

CreaturePleased.2.full: An uncanny occurrence today: I was skimming through my family's notes and found references to an experiment to procure life from death. At this same moment, I received a letter with very poor penmanship from an individual signed only as **The Creature.**

CreaturePleased.3.full: The letter reads: "I wish to alleviate some of what ails you. Even from the cold of Siberia, where I reside away from the wretched eyes of humanity, I hear word of {0} and its troubles.

CreaturePleased.4.full: I offer you this remuneration with no obligation. Your family may have cursed me, but it has also soothed the rage within me."

FOTU-End1.3.full: It feels like ages since I have written. The village that we once sojourned to all those years ago has fallen silent. It's crumbling defenses are a reminder; a metaphor for the crippling isolation of xenophobia. Even now I remember those accursed city walls that sapped my youthful vitality with every visit into the murky depths of that place; a place that could never be rebuilt after the hideous Experiment was unleashed.

FOTU-End1.4.full: Yet, even now the indomitable pull of my family's infamous work tears at my very soul! No. I cannot carry on a legacy of fear that left an entire town and estate in ruins. My colleagues at the university have no reverence for me. They laugh so heartily when I tell them the town in which I was birthed. I do not blame them. My hope is that I shall never see that foul place again. How could my family cultivate such an embarrassing line of thinking?

FOTU-End1.5.full: As I pen this note, my lawyer has made arrangements for a transfer of ownership; the deed to that wretched estate will soon finally be wrested from my hands and with it, the insidious efforts contained within will be buried forever.

FOTU-End2.3.full: I see now how wrong I had been. True inspiration, true science, true art, it emerges from isolation. Isolation is the catalyst. With silence and contemplation, the ability to truly focus without distractions, this is where perfection and enlightenment is achieved.

FOTU-End2.4.full: The citizens of {0} were right in their decision. Outside influences only pollute the mind and distract.

FOTU-End2.5.full: One must be self-reliant and self-motivated. Science is instinctual. Brilliance doesn't come from universities. No one was ever remembered as the world's greatest team player. No.

FOTU-End2.6.full: The rest of the world may be unaware of my family's work, but that is all part of my ingenious plan. Today, I retreat to my laboratory. Soon, I will emerge from my scientific cocoon more brilliant than ever before and the world will tremble at my feet!

IsoIdentification.5.full: After an extended time, I was reluctantly approved. I bundled up my papers and my wits and beat a quick path to my hansom, where the horses stamped at my approach and appeared to be just as keen as I was to leave this wretched place.

SmugEvent2ACont.4.full: Experiment Notes - A Fabric That Cannot Become Stained:

SmugEvent2ACont.5.full: While seemingly innocuous, our amazingly versatile fabric that could not be stained also appeared to have the more important side effect of repelling all possible stain sources with vicious force. Upon offering our fabric as a possible alternative for the town's flag, the light cloth explosively began to ascend and descend in mid-air, flapping wildly about the room. We fled City Hall and watched in mild amusement and terror as the experiment destroyed the building entirely within seconds.

SmugEvent2ACont.6.full: Experiment Notes - A Robot Servant That Prepares Meals with Lasers:

SmugEvent2ACont.7.full: Possibly a flawed idea from the beginning and admittedly not our best overall craftsmanship, the robot butler almost immediately began to indscriminantly fire lasers literally everywhere. Our demonstration was very brief in City Hall, before we all retreated to a safer distance and observed the easily avoidable chaos that we had caused. The City Hall was engulfed in flames in minutes. Dreadful, really.

SmugEvent2ACont.8.full: Experiment Notes - Injecting an Agitated Gorilla with Hormones and Radium:

SmugEvent2ACont.9.full: The cage in which our great primate was displayed was woefully inadequate, and upon the slightest provocation it emerged violently from its enclosure at the very beginning of our exhibition at City Hall. Covered in a disturbing amount of blood and viscera within seconds, the inevitable mistake rampaged through the room in a whirlwind of coffee and silver fur. We exited hastily to observe from a more appropriate distance as a hailstorm of shattered bones showered the nearby streets.

SmugEvent2ACont.10.full: However, undaunted, the Experiment continued its path of destruction until we were able to subdue it with our hastily prepared antidotal serum.

PEWitch2.2.full: I find with each passing evening that my parent's abhorrent obsessions boil beneath the surface of my everyday activities. Despite the village's push towards civility and the exploration of mental disabilities, I am unable to resist the clarion call of what could one day define our family's legacy!

PEWitch2.4.full: The relapse of paranoid delusion in the rural populace has made life particularly anxious for those who express a scientific aptitude. However, considering that the region's continued hysteria keeps most inhabitants locked within their ashen homes at night, fearful of every shadow that flits across the windowsill, I am reasonably sure that my new obsessions will blend into the macabre scenery unnoticed.

PEWitch2PlayerA.3.full: My lust for fame knows no boundaries. Whether fulfilled through ethical means or the mark of infamy, I was born with a yearning to be known both far and wide for my scientific exploits. These narcissistic thoughts plague my waking hours and infect my dreams!

PEWitch2PlayerA.4.full: My thirst for knowledge is unquenchable. Each evening I search through ancient tomes and scholarly texts, scouring every printed word and mathematical formula as if it were the last I will ever read.

PEWitch2PlayerA.5.full: I have spent days upon days locked away within my secret laboratory. It is as though my entire existence is singularly focused on the pursuit of scientific excellence. I do not care if it drives me mad! If my contributions can advance Science even by a minute amount it will all be worth it!

PEWitch2PlayerA.6.full: I am surrounded by simple-minded human filth. How dare they look at such an affluent individual with judgement in their eyes? How dare they interfere with an aristocrat's greatest, most valuable work? Oh, they will PAY for their insolence!

PEWitch2PlayerA.7.full: I will not suffer fools. It is just as important for a peasant or a king to know their place in the presence of my genius. I will show them **all** how to pay homage to their betters. Soon there will be no way to ignore my inspirational presence and I will command respect!

PEWitch2PlayerA.8.full: I find pleasure in the simple act of experimentation. Every tested hypothesis is a delectable morsel to be savored. And is it not my obligation - my right - to share this sense of wonder with the world? The wretches deserve to be entertained - for what is life without spectacle and indulgence?

She bid me follow her to a portion of the jail where a large section of the second floor had collapsed and we could look out over the perverted land, its dismal cracks and ruddy mires stretching out for nearly a kilometer.

JunkPalaceMeet1.4.full: {0} stood up from the table where he had been enjoying a feast and crudely wiped his lips on his stained apron. He took me aside to speak privately. As privately as we could, being surrounded by three of his most loyal followers. They carried makeshift weapons with barbed wire wrapped around cudgeled ends and wore a similar thick apron to {1}.

JunkPalaceMeet1.5.full: {0} spoke. "Since you have finally come down from your perch, I will reward you with an offer. For a minor sum, I will make sure your reputation around here is indisputable."

JunkPalaceMeet1.6.full: As you no doubt have realized from the dramatic retelling of this meeting that I have offered, I was skeptical of {0}'s tone. "I assure you, I will spread knowledge of your experiments. All of Transylvania will fear you - at least, more than they already do. I want them to *hate* you as I do."

JunkPalaceMeetb.3.full: I was anxious to leave this desolate place, so when the {0} nodded towards the exit, I sprang quickly at the opportunity and left at a brisk pace.

JunkPalaceMeetb.4.full: As I walked, {0} pointed to a large individual who remained concealed in the shadows. The Creature noticed our attention and disappeared from view. "Your family could not help that poor creature, so I have not and will not reveal to you what will befall if you do not impress me *(reach the end of the {icon:Creepy_Icon} Track)*. FOTU-End7.4.full: Demeanor: calm, distant. Not atypical for this type of rehabilitation.

FOTU-End7.5.full: Stitching area appears to have healed with no infection. Hair has begun to return around scarred area. Drill marks not noticeable.

FOTU-End8.6.full: It is my hope that this letter finds you well. The news I hear from Bucharest is positive, with a seasonable chill in the air and continued peace. As such, I pray you will indulge me in forgoing pleasantries and moving to matters of business with haste.

FOTU-End8.7.full: The institution in {0} has been an unrivaled success. A steady stream of those suffering from insanities and delusions have been shipped here from other parts of the country. Yet still officials always wonder how we run such an efficient operation even as funding remains remarkably low. I believe it is in part due to the **{1} Program** which has gained notoriety across Europe for its aggressive tactics. Those involved in the studies have shown a tremendous improvement in behavior.

FOTU-End8.8.full: Which is why I must repeat my strong request from my previous letter: we require more fresh patients to treat. Our near one hundred percent release rate has left several vacancies in the facility and we are in dire need to obtain more.

FOTU-End8.9.full: The concerns you expressed in your last letter are valid. What is the status of the released patients? How are we tracking their progress in society? How do you know we haven't simply been failing to treat them and then disposing of their bodies? Why are there bloodstains on the envelope of my previous letter? These are all important questions.

FOTU-End8.10.full: But, I ask you now; why question **results**?

TaxesEventGood.4.full: "No. No. I will take care of this misunderstanding," the man grumbled in a low and powerful voice. He produced a fountain pen from his breast pocket and with a flick of his wrist, my estate tax was excused in full.

TaxesEventGood.5.full: "As the owner of the premier lending institution in {0}, there are certain privileges I can indulge in for old friends," he stated confidentially. "Be sure to stop by some time and we can talk business."

TaxesEventGood.6.full: The creature winked, and his eye dangled from its socket with the motion. He quickly pressed it back into place with a gloved hand and made his exit before I could properly thank him. Who was that gentleman?

FOTU-End5.3.full: Sunday: I had the glorious dream again - it never fails to reinvigorate me, as I could relive that moment each night for the remainder of my years and be content.

FOTU-End5.4.full: I watch with steady eyes as my family's creation, {0}, with cathartic ambivalence, lifts the severed head of {1} high into the air. I feel the searing heat of burning oil, hear the hiss of rising steam and smoke, and smell the rusted iron in the air. The crowded arena cheered even as their leader was torn from his makeshift throne and tossed lifeless to the dusty Earth, blood pooling beneath, dark and thick as motor oil.

FOTU-End5.5.full: These images appear in my mind like light on silver even as my weathered hands strain to grasp the quill. My last act of defiance, perhaps. But what is the worth of toppling a regional tyrant? All this effort to shake the world, and barely one square kilometer has been rattled.

FOTU-End5.6.full: The inmates have moved on. The town is an empty, ruined field without vegetation; a decaying pile of ash, rust, and mud. Some days my mind feels the same. The sense of peace does nothing to stem this emptiness of purpose inside of me.

FOTU-End5.7.full: An old man visits now and then; a friend of the family with a withered face that he keeps wrapped tightly with a scarf.

FOTU-End5.8.full: What a waste contentment is! What a terrible investment! I only hope my progeny will leave this broken land behind and forge a new path.

FOTU-End6.3.full: The customs of Transylvania are even stranger than I remember. I had vague recollections from my youth of being schooled in our home and shielded from the smoky village residing deep in that valley, but I could not have guessed the true reasoning behind it all.

FOTU-End6.4.full: I have forged an alliance with the local government based on my parent's good will. They have democratically elected {0} and have even offered to provide materials and assistance for my continued experimentations. I would understand your initial apprehension at the moniker of {1}, but I assure you that the title is derived from a regional dialect and is part of tradition. They have even fashioned a gaming arena of sorts within the town proper, where a particularly aggressive form of sparring is practiced.

FOTU-End6.5.full: In fact, I find this region to be surprisingly inclusive and accepting of the avant-garde, which suits my needs as you might expect. I have even scheduled a meeting this weekend with a local Count. He claims to have been a friend of the family and has resumed interest in business ventures within the district.

FOTU-End3.3.full: If you can smell the scent of tea and rich pastries on this paper before you, it is because I write this letter to you from one of my favorite shops along the main street. The shuffling footsteps and metal din of automobiles along concrete allows my thoughts to wander. I find it disagreeably bright in these parts nowadays, but at least they serve a damn fine cuppa. There are definite benefits to traveling merchants offering a steady supply of fine goods.

FOTU-End3.4.full: It appears we have emerged from the dismal environs of yesteryear into a full springtime bloom. My family may have made a few missteps, but it seems their kind-hearted souls (of which I was not aware) won the day and assuaged the fears of the populace. I will say that it is rather enjoyable to sketch out new scientific diagrams in broad daylight without scrutiny.

FOTU-End3.5.full: There are even some willing to volunteer their time towards my "eccentric hobbies" as they call them. Such insufferable fools. I will take pleasure in exploiting their ignorance. But, I will try to be sensible about it - it is unseasonable weather for painful howling.

FOTU-End3.6.full: Anyway, send my best wishes to your mother and do not tarry too long.

FOTU-End4.3.full: It finally happened. They destroyed it all. Mobs with actual torches and pitchforks, I tell you, knocked down my properly erected fencing and stormed the estate, destroying my parents' work. The curs had the audacity to arrive unannounced; had I not heard the hounds eviscerating several members of the crowd, I may not have escaped before being swallowed up by the flames.

FOTU-End4.4.full: The grounds still remain fallow and singed by ash, enveloping the plot in a vast, dreary grayness. My entreaties to the governor have been met with indifference and ridicule. It is clear that I will receive no financial remuneration for this riotous behavior. Am I to be forever punished for the sins of my father?

FOTU-End4.5.full: No matter! What do they know of loss? I have lost everything. My family's legacy is in tatters. They drive us away as if we are the outsiders, like foreign beggars.

FOTU-End4.6.full: This is not over. I will have vengeance. This paltry village will rue the day it crossed, {0}, the Fourth!

FOTU-End4.7.full: Also, if you would be so kind as to furnish me a small loan, it would certainly expedite my ability to obtain said revenge.

CountTestResults.2.full: The patient is perfectly physically and mentally fit. I find absolutely nothing wrong with such a fine specimen of completely normal human breedstock and am utterly confused as to why they were admitted! Such sharp teeth, such glorious pallor, such divine form; why I wish all patients were so adequately equipped.

CountTestResults.3.full: Alas, despite such a **healthy**candidate for mental reformation, I must admit that they are too instrumental in the region to be confined to such dismal environs. No, I must satiate myself, and the Asylum, with others who are afflicted *(and less important)*. Release has thereby been procured upon certain private matters being addressed. It is my hope that they will provide a suitable referral in their stead.

CountTestResults.5.full: Perhaps it is unprofessional to pen my disgust upon the page, but this patient is completely undesirable for admittance. Or might I say, unfit for our institute's psychological consumption. Still, it is imperative that I negotiate the matter with the to-be-released {0} as I find myself unsatiated by this meager assessment. I am sure a referral to our glorious facility will suffice. Perhaps they know of one who is afflicted by instability - perhaps one well-fed, with rosy cheeks, and warm blood flowing through their veins.
